attribution.note: Marcus's own assertion in his post. He quotes Altman only to show what the 2016 promise was.

semantics.note: Faithfully restates a retrospective claim that a 2016 governance plan had not been carried out by publication.

contract.note: Marcus quotes the public-election plan alongside the claim, so reading 'outsiders' as publicly elected representatives is fair and ordinary. The contract correctly treats the plan as having no deadline and simply checks status at publication.

evidence.note: The original 2016 interview sets out the public-election plan. It is the baseline commitment, not evidence of the outcome.
The 2023 Form 990 shows directors are the members and elect the directors, i.e. a self-selecting board with no public electorate. Published Nov 2024, before the evaluation date.
Company disclosure from March 2024. Outside directors were added through the existing board, with no public election, consistent with the claim.

reviews.rationale: Altman described a plan for wide public election of governance representatives. The filing shows a self-perpetuating board through 2023, and the March 2024 additions were made by appointment. Nothing in the packet shows any public-election mechanism by May 2024, so the promise was not kept as of publication.

attribution.note: Marcus's own summary assertion opening his post.

semantics.note: Keeps 'lately' and both parts (mistakes and broken promises). 'A lot' has no count, and 'mistakes' is partly evaluative.

contract.note: Taking the preceding year as the period and requiring promises to be due or abandoned are fair readings. Still, with no count given and 'mistake' left undefined, the result depends on the evaluator's interpretation.

evidence.note: The superalignment compute pledge ran over four years, so it was not shown to be broken by May 2024. It neither establishes nor refutes the aggregate claim.

reviews.rationale: The packet contains one commitment, and it was not yet due. It does not establish several distinct errors or several breached promises in the period, and it does not refute them either. On this evidence the aggregate claim cannot be settled.

attribution.note: Marcus's own assertion. The Bateman quote that follows is separate and not part of this claim.

semantics.note: Accurately keeps 'massive', 'without consent' and 'in many instances without compensation'.

contract.note: Fair, ordinary reading. It separates consent from legal fair use and does not require that all material was unlicensed.

evidence.note: OpenAI's GPT-3 paper documents large web and book corpora, which establishes the scale of training data.
OpenAI's own disclosure relies on fair use plus an opt-out rather than prior permission, which is an admission against interest.
OpenAI says it mainly uses public data and does not pay for public information, consistent with many uses being uncompensated.
The NYT complaint, a party's assertion, says Times content was used without permission or payment. OpenAI's disclosure confirms the content was used.

reviews.rationale: OpenAI's own documents show training on very large web and book corpora, reliance on fair use and opt-out instead of permission, and no payment for public data. A major rights holder documents use of its content without permission or payment. Together these support large-scale training on copyrighted material without consent, with many uses uncompensated.

attribution.note: Marcus's own assertion in the post.

semantics.note: Mostly faithful. It softens 'specifically told them not to' slightly. The 'dismissive attitude' part is an evaluative judgment that cannot be scored.

contract.note: Distinguishing when the voice was created from when it was deployed, and a refusal to participate from an express prohibition, is a reasonable reading of 'make' and 'told them not to', and the contract allows a mixed result. But the outcome does turn on that distinction.

evidence.note: NPR reports that the demo voice sounded much like Johansson, which supports recognizable resemblance.
OpenAI's account (a company disclosure) puts casting and recording in mid-2023, before her refusal in September 2023.
Secondary reporting of the Washington Post's document review backs up casting before outreach to Johansson.
Johansson's statement confirms she declined the offer. It does not show that she forbade a similar voice.

reviews.rationale: Holds: the voice resembled Johansson, she declined OpenAI's offer, and OpenAI still demoed the voice with GPT-4o afterwards. Fails: the evidence indicates the voice was cast and recorded before she refused, and nothing shows she specifically told them not to use a similar voice. The attitude judgment is not scorable.
